facts.fact: The platform piloted from 10 August 2025 enables local administrations in the federal member states to begin digitally registering births, deaths, marriages and divorces, according to the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation.

Local administrations in Jubbaland, Southwest, Hirshabelle, Galmudug and Northeastern State register events digitally on the platform and all records are stored in a centralised national database, as the ministry announced on 10 August 2025.

The service was launched as a pilot in 19 districts across five federal member states on 10 August 2025, with no total number of districts or offices given; SONNA, as cited, calls it functional in 19 districts and to be rolled out nationwide.

The pilot was announced by the Ministry of Interior, Federal Affairs and Reconciliation, which is testing interfaces to integrate the platform with health, education, national ID and immigration services.

A government roadmap sets out plans to scale the service to every district, including remote and underserved areas, subject to funding and infrastructure; the document gives the roadmap no date, so its publication date of 11 August 2025 is used.

UNICEF, partnering with the government and Germany, supported the foundational work and, by its own account, 19 districts were equipped with registration tools under the pilot, including tablets for health facilities without computers; no domestic budget line is stated and scale-up is subject to funding.
The Unified Digital Civil Registration Service was launched as a pilot in 19 districts on Africa CRVS Day, 10 August 2025.
